The candidate sends primary Unicode code 65 with alt+shift. The linked Kitty document explicitly uses the unshifted primary code 97 and forbids 65 for that shifted-key example. Existing source controls accept 65, and the issue asks to preserve decoded printable metadata; the scope of that extension requires a contract decision. Do not silently assume the packet is standard-conforming.
